name: select
description: Choose one option from a fixed set. A few options are shown as radio buttons, all in view; more are a dropdown. One component either way, so what a person picks and what is stored are the same.

use.when: one choice from a fixed set: a status, a kind, a period.
use.not: free text, which is a text-field; several choices, which are checkboxes; a record out of hundreds, which is a lookup.

label.description: The question: the legend of the radios, or the dropdown's label.

options.title: Choices
options.description: Either plain strings, shown as-is, or objects {value, label} when what is stored differs from what a person should read.

as.title: Shown as
as.description: auto shows five or fewer options as radios, all in view, and more as a dropdown. radios or dropdown when the author knows better, such as a dropdown in a table cell.

a11y.role: group of radios under its question (a fieldset with a legend) for a few options; combobox (a native select) for more

keyboard.does: moves focus to the chosen radio, or to the dropdown, and on
among radios, chooses the next or previous; in a dropdown, moves between options
chooses the focused radio, or opens the dropdown
in an open dropdown, chooses the highlighted option

wcag.notes: Native radios and a native select, so every platform's assistive technology already supports them. Radios sit in a fieldset whose legend is the question, so each is read as an answer to it (1.3.1), and each label is part of its 44px target (2.5.5). No custom dropdown.

machine.identify: data-as says radios or dropdown. Radios: input[type=radio], each with the stored value, labelled by the text a person reads; the legend is the question. Dropdown: a select whose options carry the value and the text.
machine.operate: Radios: check the input whose value is wanted. Dropdown: set the select's value to one of the option values.
